LFNTSR - long file names for MS-DOS
===================================

LFNTSR gives DOS 3.10 and newer the long file name functions of
Windows 95 (INT 21h, functions 71xxh) on FAT12 and FAT16 disks, which
NewShell16 uses for long file names. It runs on any PC, 8086 and 286
included, and takes about 23 KB of memory (19 KB with /T:0; it can be
loaded high with LH). The long names are stored as Windows 95 stores them, so Windows 95,
Linux and mtools read them too.

NewShell16 Setup adds this line to AUTOEXEC.BAT when "Long file names in
DOS" is chosen (and removes it again when the option is turned off or
NewShell16 is removed):

  C:\NEWSHELL\LFNTSR\LFNTSR.COM /Q

  LFNTSR [/U] [/F] [/Q] [/H:n] [/T:n]
    /U    uninstall
    /F    install even if another long file name driver is there
    /Q    quiet
    /H:n  find handles, 1-64 (default 8)
    /T:n  long names remembered for tunnelling, 0-32 (default 8; 0 off)

LFNTSR is free software under the GNU General Public License, version 3
or later (COPYING.TXT in the NewShell16 directory). Its source is in SRC\
(NASM: nasm -f bin -I SRC\ -o LFNTSR.COM SRC\LFNTSR.ASM) and at
https://github.com/ceisserer/lnf286 (this build: commit @COMMIT@).

Good to know:

  - Programs for MS-DOS and Windows 3.1 only know the 8.3 names. Like
    Windows 95, LFNTSR keeps their long names anyway ("tunnelling"): a
    file deleted or renamed by its 8.3 name and created again under the
    same 8.3 name in the same directory within 15 seconds gets its long
    name and creation time back (Write's Save As, temp file + rename
    saves), and the long name entries of files deleted or renamed by 8.3
    name are removed, so none stay behind on the disk.
  - Network drives, CD-ROMs and FAT32 drives get 8.3 names only.
  - Windows for Workgroups 3.11: turn 32-bit file access off
    (Control Panel > 386 Enhanced > Virtual Memory > Change) when LFNTSR
    is used; Windows' own file system would bypass it. 32-bit disk access
    can stay on.
  - Windows programs that call the long file name functions from
    protected mode get 8.3 names (NewShell16 calls them in real mode
    and is not affected).
